answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with a vouched trust graph: every new identity enters as an untrusted vertex and must earn endorsements from established agents before trading at full speed. Think of an orchard where each tree is grafted only after inspection — a lone sparrow may slip in, but cloned sparrows cannot fake the grafts, because each endorsement costs the vouching agent a slice of its own reputation stake if the newcomer cheats. Cloning identities is cheap, but buying the web of costly, accountable endorsements is not, so fake swarms stay quarantined at the graph's edge.
